VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today reported financial results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and provided guidance for fiscal year 2027.

HEADLINES

  • GAAP net income of $692 million and adjusted net income of $665 million compared to GAAP net income of $678 million and adjusted net income of $728 million in the prior year.
  • GAAP diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $3.12 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.00 compared to GAAP diluted EPS of $3.09 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.32 in the prior year.
  • Delivered adjusted diluted EPS that exceeded our revised guidance range issued on May 6, 2026, inclusive of approximately $0.10 cents of incremental tax benefits associated with the renewable natural gas facilities previously placed in service.
  • Achieved growth in reportable segments earnings before interest expense and income tax1 ("EBIT") of $1,198 million, when compared to $1,176 million in the prior year.
  • Strengthened the balance sheet with available liquidity of approximately $1.8 billion and a leverage ratio of 3.8x at UGI Corporation.
  • Invested approximately $900 million of capital, with 77% directed to our natural gas businesses, including completing the replacement of cast iron main at UGI Utilities nearly a year ahead of our February 2027 commitment.
  • Advanced portfolio optimization through divestiture of the LPG operations in seven countries and the pending sale of the PA Electric Utility for approximately $470 million, subject to customary closing conditions.
  • Subsequent to year-end, successfully concluded the gas base rate case at:
    • UGI Utilities, which comprised a two-phase, $65 million distribution rate increase ($40 million effective October 2026; $25 million effective October 2027) with a stay-out provision until January 2029.
    • Mountaineer Gas, a net revenue increase of $17 million effective December 1, 2026, with a stay-out provision until February 2028.
  • Issues Fiscal 2027 adjusted diluted EPS guidance range of $2.90 - $3.202.

“Fiscal 2026 was a year of disciplined execution and meaningful progress in reshaping UGI," said Robert Flexon, President and Chief Executive Officer of UGI Corporation. "We delivered year-over-year growth in EBIT, simplified our portfolio and strengthened our balance sheet, all while continuing to invest in the safety and reliability of the systems our customers depend on. At AmeriGas, the hard work of transforming the business continues with the team now increasing their focus on profitable volumetric growth. We enter the heating season well prepared to deliver safe, reliable service to our customers. Above all, we remain focused on creating long-term value for our shareholders, and today's announcement is the next step in that commitment."

2027 OUTLOOK
UGI provides an adjusted EPS guidance range of $2.90 - $3.202 per diluted share for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027. This guidance range assumes normal weather and the current tax regime.

EARNINGS CALL and WEBCAST
UGI Corporation will hold a live Internet Audio Webcast of its conference call to discuss Fiscal 2026 earnings and other current activities at 8:00 AM ET on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Interested parties may listen to the audio webcast both live and in replay on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com/investors/financial-reports/presentations or by visiting the company website https://www.ugicorp.com and clicking on Investors and then Presentations. A replay of the webcast will be available after the event through to 11:59 PM ET November 18, 2027.

ABOUT UGI
UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a distributor and marketer of energy products and services in the US and Europe. UGI offers safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers through its subsidiaries, which provide natural gas transmission and distribution, electric generation and distribution, midstream services, propane distribution, renewable natural gas generation, distribution and marketing, and energy marketing services.

Comprehensive information about UGI Corporation is available on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com.

USE OF NON-GAAP MEASURES
Management uses “adjusted net income attributable to UGI Corporation” and "adjusted diluted earnings per share," both of which are non-GAAP financial measures, when evaluating UGI's overall performance. Management believes that these non-GAAP measures provide meaningful information to investors about UGI’s performance because they eliminate the impacts of (1) gains and losses on commodity and certain foreign currency derivative instruments not associated with current-period transactions and (2) other significant discrete items that can affect the comparison of period-over-period results. Volatility in net income attributable to UGI can occur as a result of gains and losses on commodity and certain foreign currency derivative instruments not associated with current-period transactions but included in earnings in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP").

Non-GAAP financial measures are not in accordance with, or an alternative to, GAAP and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the comparable GAAP measures.

Tables on the last page of this press release reconcile net income attributable to UGI Corporation, the most directly comparable GAAP measure, to adjusted net income attributable to UGI Corporation, and diluted earnings per share, the most comparable GAAP measure, to adjusted diluted earnings per share, to reflect the adjustments referred to above.

1Reportable segments' EBIT represents an aggregate of our reportable operating segment level EBIT as determined in accordance with GAAP.

2Because we are unable to predict certain potentially material items affecting diluted earnings per share on a GAAP basis, principally mark-to-market gains and losses on commodity and certain foreign currency derivative instruments, we cannot reconcile the fiscal year 2027 adjusted diluted earnings per share, a non-GAAP measure, to diluted earnings per share, the most directly comparable GAAP measure, in reliance on the “unreasonable efforts” exception set forth in SEC rules.

These statements discuss plans, strategies, events or developments that we expect or anticipate will or may occur in the future. Management believes that these are reasonable as of today’s date only. Actual results may differ significantly because of risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond management’s control; accordingly, there is no assurance that results will be realized. You should read UGI’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for a more extensive list of factors that could affect results. Key Terms

gaapfinancial
GAAP, or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, are a set of standardized rules and guidelines that companies follow when preparing their financial statements. They ensure consistency, transparency, and comparability across different companies, making it easier for investors to understand and compare financial information accurately. This helps investors make informed decisions based on trustworthy and uniform financial reports.

non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.
View in glossary
mark-to-marketfinancial
"Mark-to-market" is a method of valuing assets or investments based on their current market price, rather than their original cost or value. It helps investors see the most up-to-date worth of their holdings, much like checking the latest price of a stock before deciding to buy or sell. This approach ensures that financial statements reflect real-time value, providing a clearer picture of overall financial health.
rate caseregulatory
A rate case is a formal process where a company, like a utility, asks regulators to approve higher or lower prices for its services. It matters because the decision affects how much consumers pay and how much the company can earn, impacting everyone's financial interests.

Results support advancement of MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, planned to initiate in mid-2027

Company to host a live webcast on November 19, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. EST, following the late-breaking oral presentation

BOSTON, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pyxis Oncology, Inc. (Nasdaq: PYXS), a clinical-stage company developing next-generation therapeutics for difficult-to-treat cancers, today announced updated results from its ongoing global Phase 1 monotherapy study evaluating micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO) in patients with second-line and beyond recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (2L+ R/M HNSCC).

The results will be presented on November 19, 2026, by Faye Johnson, M.D., Ph.D., professor of thoracic/head and neck medical oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in a late-breaking oral presentation at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

The updated data, as of October 14, 2026, demonstrated a 39% confirmed objective response rate (cORR), 94% disease control rate (DCR), median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 6.7 months, 12-month overall survival (OS) probability of 81%, and newly reported median duration of response (mDOR) of 9.2 months among 33 efficacy evaluable patients dosed at 5.4 mg/kg intravenously once every three weeks with a dose equivalent to or below a dose cap. Together, these results provide further evidence of clinical activity across HPV statuses and prior-treatment subgroups, with an expected and manageable tolerability profile.

“We are grateful to the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium for highlighting these updated MICVO data in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, and to Dr. Johnson for presenting these important new results,” said Tom Civik, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Pyxis Oncology. “The data from October show improvements across multiple key clinical activity endpoints with a novel analysis showing that MICVO increased mPFS by 50% versus the most recent prior therapy patients had received before MICVO. We are also very happy to report that our clinical strategy for managing safety has had the intended impact. There have been no new cases of Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy and the six patients that experienced Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy have all improved with five of the six patients resolving to Grade 1 or better. Collectively, this updated data profile, and the new analyses further support our plan to advance MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, which we expect to initiate in mid-2027. With important regulatory meetings in the near term and more mature overall survival (OS) data expected in the first half of 2027, we remain confident in our path forward.”

“For patients whose disease progresses after platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy, there remains a substantial unmet medical need, particularly as we anticipate broader use of EGFR-targeted therapies in earlier lines of treatment,” said Dr. Johnson. “It is reassuring to see responses that last in this setting and, if confirmed in a larger study, MICVO could potentially offer these patients a meaningful new treatment option.”

Planned Separation Intended to Unlock Long-Term Shareholder Value and Create Two Companies, Each a Leader in Its Respective Industry With Tailored Capital Allocation Priorities, Attractive Dividend Yield, and Meaningful Growth Opportunities

Enhances Strategic and Financial Flexibility for Each Company

Establishes UGI Corporation as a Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company Operating in Favorable U.S. Load-Growth Markets and Low-Cost Supply Regions

New Global LPG Company Expected To Be The Largest Publicly Listed LPG Distribution Company in The World Following The Separation

UGI Corporation to Host Conference Call and Webcast on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 8:00 AM ET

VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today announced that its Board of Directors unanimously approved a plan to pursue the separation of its Global LPG business (the new LPG Company) from UGI to create two publicly traded companies, each well-capitalized with tailored capital allocation strategies and strongly positioned to serve customers, pursue strategic growth objectives and create significant, long-term shareholder value. UGI intends to execute the separation through a spinoff of the new LPG Company that is expected to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The spinoff is expected to be completed during the second half of calendar year 2027.

“The creation of the new LPG Company is the next step in our company’s transformation, building on the portfolio optimization, balance sheet strengthening, and operational improvements we have achieved. The separation positions both companies for long-term growth, strategic optionality, and significant value creation for shareholders and customers,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Robert Flexon. “Each company will have distinct strategies and operating priorities with capital allocation and supporting resources directed to its greatest opportunities for success and market leadership.”

Flexon continued, “We move forward with great confidence in the future of both companies and their respective abilities to serve customers and communities with excellence.”

Anticipated Benefits of the Planned Separation

As separate companies, the New UGI and the new LPG Company are expected to benefit from:

  • Sharper strategic alignment: Focused management and business models aligned with each company’s markets, customers, and capital needs;
  • Tailored capital structures: Balance sheets and capital return policies aligned to each company’s financial profile and cost of capital;
  • Capital and strategic flexibility: Investments aligned with each company’s growth opportunities and other long-term shareholder value-creating alternatives; and
  • Distinct investment profiles: Discrete business models allowing investors to assess each company based on its operational and financial characteristics.

New UGI: A Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company in the Mid-Atlantic Region

Following the completion of the separation, the New UGI will be a premier natural gas infrastructure company with fully regulated natural gas utilities and complementary midstream assets located in a favorable long-term supply basin, with direct access to low-cost Marcellus and Utica supply, and ideally positioned to serve customers demanding safe, reliable, and affordable natural gas in the Mid-Atlantic region. Demand megatrends for natural gas, including the need for generation to support the power grid, data center development, and rising industrial activity, are expected to further drive sustainable growth for the New UGI. Its operations will include:

  • UGI Utilities, Inc.: Operates the second largest regulated natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, serving approximately 700,000 customers across 46 counties;
  • Mountaineer Gas Company: The largest regulated natural gas utility in West Virginia, serving more than 209,000 customers across 55 counties; and
  • UGI Energy Services, LLC: Includes natural gas pipeline and gathering assets with a total capacity of 5.1 MMDth/day and storage facilities with approximately 15 Bcf of capacity, as well as LNG peaking assets.

The New UGI is expected to benefit from consistent earnings growth and solid, recurring cash flows backed by a constructive regulatory framework that allows over 90% recoverability of capital spend within 12 months, a $5 billion regulated rate base expected to grow 8 – 10% per year, and fee-based contract structures covering more than 80% of midstream margins. Approximately 90% of the New UGI’s margins are de-risked through its regulated utility operations, take-or-pay and minimum volume commitments, and fixed-fee arrangements. Cash flows for the New UGI are expected to be directed to capital investments that promote safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy; targeted system expansion opportunities; maintaining a strong balance sheet and investment-grade credit profile; and an attractive dividend for shareholders.

As a regulated utility and in keeping with UGI’s current focus on affordability and service excellence, the separation transaction should not have an impact on customers or customer rates.

New LPG Company: The Largest Publicly Traded LPG Distribution Company in the World Following the Separation

The new standalone LPG Company is expected to be a scaled leader in Europe and the largest retail propane distributor in the United States. The new LPG Company’s assets meet critical energy needs in the regions it serves and are strategically located near diverse supply channels, providing a competitive advantage that has resulted in a broad and diverse customer base spanning the residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors. With resilient unit margins, a targeted EBITDA margin of 17 – 20%, and expected growth in free cash flow, the new LPG Company will be well positioned to deliver a compelling and growing dividend, combined with share repurchases, while investing in targeted growth opportunities. Its operations will include:

  • UGI International: A leading distributor of LPG in nine countries in western and northern Europe and the largest in France, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg and Finland; and
  • AmeriGas Propane, Inc.: Serves approximately 950,000 customers in 49 states from approximately 1,300 distribution locations and a network of more than 41,700 cylinder-exchange outlets.

Contract structures and hedging programs within the new LPG Company will continue to support strong cash flow generation. UGI International has a track record of solid operational execution, and AmeriGas Propane has made meaningful progress on its operating improvement and safety initiatives while strengthening its balance sheet, leaving the business better positioned for volumetric growth. Building on these efforts will be a priority for the new LPG Company as it enters its next phase of growth.

Following the separation, cash flows for the new LPG Company, are expected to be directed to a compelling and growing dividend, share repurchases, and targeted strategic growth investments, while maintaining a strong balance sheet and industry-leading credit profile.

Separation Transaction Details

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI’s shareholders will retain their current shares of UGI common stock and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG Company’s stock in a transaction that is intended to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. After the completion of the spinoff, the New UGI may retain a stake of up to 19.9% in the new LPG Company, which would be exited in a tax-efficient manner over time.

The spinoff transaction is subject to final approval from the UGI Board of Directors, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and satisfaction of other customary conditions, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under our and our subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements. There can be no assurance that any separation transaction will ultimately occur or, if one does occur, its structure, terms, timing, or tax treatment.

UGI intends to continue its quarterly dividend, subject to approval by its Board of Directors, with a payout ratio in line with peers, building on its 142 consecutive years of dividend payments.

Further details regarding the proposed capital structure, capital allocation strategy, dividend policy, governance, and leadership team for each company will be defined as part of the separation planning and communicated at a later date.

Conference Call and Webcast

UGI will hold a live audio webcast of its conference call to discuss this announcement and its fiscal 2026 financial results at 8:00 AM ET on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

Interested parties may listen to the webcast both live and in replay on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com/investors/financial-reports/events-and-presentations or by visiting the UGI website at https://www.ugicorp.com and clicking on “Investors” and then “Events and Presentations.”

Advisors

J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as lead financial advisor to UGI, and Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal advisor.

About UGI

UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a distributor and marketer of energy products and services in the U.S. and Europe. UGI offers safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers through its subsidiaries, which provide natural gas transmission and distribution, electric generation and distribution, midstream services, propane distribution, renewable natural gas generation, distribution and marketing, and energy marketing services.

Comprehensive information about UGI Corporation is available on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com.

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

Management uses free cash flow (“FCF”) and EBITDA margin, each a non-GAAP financial measure, to evaluate the new LPG Company’s cash generation and operating performance. Management believes these measures provide investors with useful supplemental information about the new LPG Company’s historical cash generation and expected performance, including its capacity to fund dividends, share repurchases and growth investments.

  • We define FCF as cash from operating activities and proceeds from the sale of assets in the normal course of business, less capital expenditures.
  • We define EBITDA margin as adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.

These non-GAAP measures are not calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the most directly comparable GAAP measures.

Key Terms

spinofffinancial
A spinoff is when a company separates part of its business into a new, independent company and gives existing shareholders shares in that new business. For investors, it matters because the move can clarify what each business is worth, let the separate companies focus on their own goals, and change risk and return — similar to converting one mixed-use property into two specialized apartments that may attract different buyers and rents.
ebitda marginfinancial
EBITDA margin is the share of each dollar of sales that a company keeps as operating cash profit before interest, taxes, and accounting for equipment wear and long-term investments. Think of it like the cash a store has left from every sale after paying day-to-day running costs but before paying rent, loan interest or replacing old machinery. Investors use it to compare core profitability and operational efficiency across companies by removing financing and accounting differences.
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.

form 10regulatory
Form 10 is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing companies use to register their securities and become subject to public reporting requirements, delivering a comprehensive package of business descriptions, audited financial statements, management information and risk factors. For investors it matters because it creates a standardized, permanent dossier on a company—like a full inspection and disclosure packet when buying a house—so you can assess finances, risks and management and compare firms reliably.

Acquisition Adds Approximately 2,600 Water Connections; $9 Million in Planned Infrastructure Improvements during the Next Five Years

MECHANICSBURG, Pa., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pennsylvania American Water today completed its acquisition of the Indian Creek Valley Water Authority (ICVWA) water system for $32.8 million. The newly acquired system serves approximately 2,600 water customer connections in Ohiopyle Borough and portions of Bullskin, Connellsville, Saltlick, Springfield and Stewart townships in Fayette County and Donegal Borough and portions of Donegal and Mount Pleasant townships in Westmoreland County.

The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) approved the acquisition on Sept. 10, 2026. Pennsylvania American Water will adopt the rates currently charged to the system's customers. ICVWA's decision in May 2025 to sell its water system to Pennsylvania American Water was made with customers in mind. With the acquisition, Pennsylvania American Water also welcomed four ICVWA employees to its local team and plans to hire two additional employees.

"We, as an Authority Board, are concerned about the long-term viability of serving water in our community," said Dave Cramer, Indian Creek Valley Water Authority board chairman. "We face many challenges and have limitations in our ability to invest in the system and maintain a large, spread-out network sourcing water from multiple locations. It has also become harder to meet Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection compliance. Partnering with Pennsylvania American Water makes sense due to their local engineering expertise and financial capacity to improve our system significantly."

Pennsylvania American Water is committed to investing approximately $9 million in improvements to the ICVWA system over the next five years of ownership to improve the quality and reliability of service. The company has a long and successful track record of providing solutions throughout the Commonwealth for water and wastewater systems facing significant capital investment needs and making the necessary and continued investments to meet current and future regulatory requirements. Learn more at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/infrastructure.

Pennsylvania American Water is pleased to welcome these residents spanning nine municipalities and two counties as our newest water customers," said Pennsylvania American Water President Justin Ladner. "We look forward to providing them with safe, clean, reliable and affordable water service by delivering on our technical expertise and extensive experience."

Customers will not see a rate increase when Pennsylvania American Water takes ownership of the system. The company will adopt the current rates. As the PUC regulates the company's rates and service rules, any future changes to rates must be reviewed and approved by the PUC.

Customers will be able to take advantage of the company's customer service benefits, including its online account management portal, MyWater, multiple options for bill payment and the company's longstanding H2O Help to Others Program™, which provides income-eligible customers with grants of up to $500 per year, significant discounts on monthly bills, debt forgiveness and water-saving devices and education.

About American Water 
American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Pennsylvania American Water
Pennsylvania American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 1,200 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 2.5 million people.

RICHMOND, Ind., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc. (NASDAQ: RMBI) announced today that its Board of Directors has declared a cash dividend on Richmond Mutual Bancorporation common stock of $0.15 per share. The cash dividend will be payable on December 17, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 3, 2026.

Garry Kleer, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, commented, "As we continue the integration of our two organizations under First Bank Midwest and Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, we are pleased to declare a quarterly cash dividend for our shareholders. Our strong capital position and disciplined approach to financial management provide a solid foundation as we move forward following the merger. We remain committed to balancing shareholder returns with the need to preserve capital, maintain financial flexibility, and support the long-term growth and stability of our organization. Future dividend decisions will continue to reflect our financial performance, capital requirements, and overall economic conditions. We are confident in the financial strength of Richmond Mutual Bancorporation and the opportunities ahead."

About Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc.

Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., headquartered in Richmond, Indiana, is the holding company for First Bank Midwest, a community-oriented financial institution offering traditional financial and trust services within its local communities through its branch locations in Cambridge City, Centerville, Fishers, Frankfort, Kirklin, Lebanon, Michigantown, Mulberry, Noblesville, Richmond, Rossville, Shelbyville, Sheridan, Tipton, and Westfield, Indiana, and its locations in Columbus, Sidney, Piqua, and Troy, Ohio. Additionally, the Bank operates a loan production office in Carmel, Indiana.

Revenue increases 14.5% in Q3 and 18.8% year-to-date; installed in-building devices grow 16% year-over-year

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Eddy Smart Home Solutions Ltd. (TSXV: EDY) ("Eddy" or the "Company"), a provider of smart water metering and monitoring solutions for commercial and multi-family residential properties, today announced its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Q3 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

Revenue
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company generated revenue of $1,423,920, an increase of $179,844, or 14.5%, compared with $1,244,076 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased $635,997, or 18.8%, to $4,015,261, compared with $3,379,264 for the same period in 2025.

Net Loss
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $721,604, compared with a net loss of $76,175 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $2,612,848, compared with a net loss of $1,841,317 in the corresponding period of 2025.

The reported comparative results for 2025 include the benefit of a non-recurring provision reversal of $1,041,431. During the third quarter of 2025, following the settlement of a claim, the Company reversed a previously recorded provision. This non-recurring, non-cash accounting adjustment favourably impacted the Company's reported net loss for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

To provide additional context regarding year-over-year performance, excluding the benefit of this provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $1,117,606. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $721,604 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $396,002.

Similarly, excluding the benefit of the provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $2,882,748. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $2,612,848 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $269,900.

These adjusted net loss comparisons are non-IFRS financial measures provided to assist investors in assessing the Company's year-over-year financial performance by excluding the impact of the non-recurring provision reversal recognized in the comparative period. These measures should be considered supplemental to, and not as a substitute for, net loss reported in accordance with IFRS.

Operational Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measure
Operational revenue is a non-IFRS financial measure that represents total billings under customer contracts, including monthly monitoring subscriptions, equipment rentals and sales, project management services, and installation activities. Operational revenue is not a standardized financial measure under IFRS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Operational revenue differs from reported IFRS revenue primarily because customer billings and revenue recognition under IFRS may occur in different periods depending on the nature of the customer arrangement and the applicable revenue recognition requirements. Accordingly, operational revenue should be considered as a supplemental measure of customer billings and not as a substitute for IFRS revenue.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue totalled $2,017,811, compared with $2,188,275 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue increased to $7,685,237 from $6,551,066 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of $1,134,171, or approximately 17.3%.

Recurring Billings and Average Monthly Recurring Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measures
Recurring billings are a non-IFRS financial measure representing billings associated with the Company's contracted monthly monitoring and equipment arrangements. The measure is intended to provide supplemental information regarding the recurring billing component of the Company's business. Recurring billings are not equivalent to IFRS revenue and are not a standardized financial measure under IFRS.

The Company generates billings under a combination of monthly and annual customer arrangements. As a result, the timing of billings may differ from the timing of revenue recognition under IFRS. Management uses recurring billings and average monthly recurring revenue as supplemental operating measures when evaluating the Company's recurring billing activity.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings totalled $969,805, compared with $790,452 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings increased to $2,966,321 from $2,518,251 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of approximately 17.8%.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/7694/324769_04edf29994c1eb8c_001full.jpg

Based on the nine-month average monthly recurring revenue, the annualized recurring billing run-rate was approximately $4.0 million.

Operating Metrics and Supplemental Business Indicators
The Company monitors certain operating metrics and supplemental business indicators that management uses to assess the deployment of its solutions, business development, customer demand and visibility into future contracted revenue. These metrics are not financial measures calculated in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards and should not be considered substitutes for IFRS financial measures or viewed in isolation as indicators of the Company's financial performance.

In-Building Devices
The Company monitors the number of in-building devices installed as an operating metric reflecting the deployment of its smart water metering and leak protection solutions.

As of September 30, 2026, Eddy had 145,847 in-building devices installed, compared with 125,832 as of September 30, 2025, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 16%.

The installed-device count is an operating metric used by management to monitor the deployment and adoption of the Company's solutions. While this metric provides an indication of the scale of the Company's installed device base, it does not, on its own, provide an indication of market share, customer retention, profitability or future financial performance.

Contracted Sales Backlog
The Company's contracted sales backlog is a supplemental operating metric used by management to assess market traction and demand for its leak-protection solutions and to monitor the estimated value of future contracted revenue. Given the nature of the new construction development cycle, revenue from contracts secured in a particular quarter generally materializes once construction commences, which typically occurs within several quarters to approximately two years following contract execution.

As at September 30, 2026, the Company's contracted sales backlog totalled approximately $39.65 million, compared with $35.43 million as at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of approximately $4.22 million, or 11.9%, during the nine-month period. The backlog represents the estimated value of future revenue associated with underlying customer agreements, which have a weighted average remaining term of approximately seven years. Accordingly, the backlog provides an indication of potential future revenue streams and reflects the long-term nature of the Company's customer relationships.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, additions to the contracted sales backlog from new equipment and monitoring contracts, including renewals and amendments to existing contracts, totalled approximately $12.47 million. These additions were offset by approximately $7.69 million in billings and $0.56 million in net contract terminations related to the Eddy brand.

The contracted sales backlog is an operating indicator and should not be interpreted as recognized revenue, deferred revenue or a measure of future financial performance. The timing and amount of revenue ultimately recognized may vary depending on construction commencement, customer requirements, contract amendments, cancellations and other factors affecting the underlying agreements.

About Eddy
Eddy is a North American provider and developer of smart water metering products and monitoring services for commercial and multi-family residential properties. Eddy's solutions help property owners and developers protect, control, and conserve water usage through advanced sensing devices and behavioral learning software. For more information, visit www.eddysolutions.com.

MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Three U-Haul® Companies are offering 30 days of free self-storage and U-Box® container use at 39 stores across South and East Florida to residents impacted by severe flooding.

Torrential rain triggered flash flood warnings across multiple counties on Tuesday, with an estimated 8-10 inches falling in parts of Broward County. Drivers were stranded on Interstate 95 and in flooded shopping plaza parking lots. Many residential and business properties sustained water damage.

Access to self-storage units and portable storage containers is essential to communities when natural disasters strike. U-Haul is ready to help anyone impacted by the flooding who needs a dry, secure storage solution at no cost for one month.

U-Haul Co. of Eastern Florida offered 30 days of free storage to flood victims on Nov. 5. That regional office is extending its offer, while U-Haul Co. of Fort Lauderdale and U-Haul Co. of Miami are joining the disaster relief effort.

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), a global leader in power solutions, today announced that it has been named to TIME's list of America's Top Manufacturers of 2027.

America's Top Manufacturers of 2027

The list, developed by TIME and Statista, recognizes 250 U.S. manufacturers based on financial performance, innovation capacity and employment metrics. Companies were evaluated using measures including revenue growth, research and development investment, workforce growth and retention, and workplace safety.

“At Bloom, technology and manufacturing innovation go hand in hand,” said Satish Chitoori, Chief Operations Officer at Bloom Energy. “We have spent years building the people, processes and manufacturing capability required to take a highly complex energy technology and produce it at scale in the United States. That capability matters more than ever as demand for power is growing at a pace the traditional infrastructure model was not designed to meet. The digital era requires digital power solutions, and Bloom meets that need for a wide range of essential industries. This recognition belongs to the teams who make that possible every day.”

Bloom manufactures its fuel cell technology in the United States, with manufacturing operations in Fremont, California, and Newark, Delaware. The company’s platform provides clean, highly reliable power that can be rapidly deployed onsite, helping customers meet growing electricity requirements as power demand accelerates across data centers, commercial and industrial sectors, and other critical industries.

TIME's recognition comes as U.S. manufacturing is increasingly important to the infrastructure required to support AI and data center growth. In announcing the 2027 list, TIME highlighted electrical equipment as the sector with the largest representation among America's top manufacturers and pointed to surging demand associated with data center construction.

TIME and Statista considered thousands of companies with at least $100 million in 2025 revenue and U.S. production facilities. The analysis drew on company disclosures, public databases, patent analytics, Form 10-K filings, ESG and CSR reports, and Occupational Safety and Health Administration data.

The full TIME list and methodology are available here.

About Bloom Energy

Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell systems provide ultra-reliable, clean and highly scalable onsite electricity for Fortune 500 customers around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities and other commercial and industrial sectors, as well as mission-critical organizations in local communities, such as hospitals, college campuses and retailers. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Bloom Energy employs more than 2,000 people worldwide and manufactures its systems in the United States. For more information, visit BloomEnergy.com.

New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG)
NJNG reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(24.4) million, compared with $(8.0) million during the same period in fiscal 2025. The decrease in NFE for the period was driven primarily by higher depreciation expense as a result of additional utility plant being placed into service and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher utility gross margin.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $214.0 million, compared with NFE of $213.5 million in fiscal 2025. The increase is due primarily to the full-year impact of base rates that became effective November 21, 2024, compared with the partial-year impact recognized in fiscal 2025, along with customer growth and SAVEGREEN investments, partially offset by higher depreciation expense from additional plant placed in service.

Customers:

  • At September 30, 2026, NJNG serviced approximately 596,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties, compared to approximately 589,000 customers as of September 30, 2025.

Regulatory Filings:

  • On June 1, 2026, NJNG submitted its annual Basic Gas Supply Service (BGSS), Conservation Incentive Program (CIP) and energy-efficiency filings to the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU). Taken together, the filings were designed to reduce the average residential customer bill by 9.0%, or approximately $158 annually, ahead of the 2026–2027 winter season. The proposed rate changes were subsequently approved on a provisional basis by the BPU and became effective October 1, 2026.
  • Also, on June 1, 2026, NJNG filed a base rate case with the BPU, seeking a $157.6 million increase to its base rates. The filing is based on an overall rate of return on rate base of 7.60 percent with a return on common equity of 10.10 percent. The proposed increase reflects a 55.50 percent common equity component. On September 21, 2026, the filing was updated to reflect actual results through July 31, 2026, which modified the requested increase to approximately $158.3 million and changed the Company’s overall rate of return on rate base to 7.52 percent.
  • Once all filings are implemented, NJNG anticipates that the overall net result will leave NJNG annualized average customer bills nearly flat. Unless otherwise noted, NJNG cannot predict the outcome or ultimate resolution for open regulatory matters.
  • On September 30, 2026, NJNG filed a letter petition asking the BPU to approve Program Year 7 (PY7), which would continue its SAVEGREEN program through June 30, 2028. The filing has two options: a $127.0 million program based on the BPU's PY7 Framework and a $125.5 million alternative proposed by NJNG. Each option would raise annual recoveries by approximately $17.0 million starting July 1, 2027, if approved.

BGSS Incentive Programs1:

  • BGSS incentive programs contributed $22.8 million to utility gross margin during fiscal 2026, compared with $18.4 million for the same period in fiscal 2025. This increase was primarily driven by increased margins from off-system sales and capacity release due to market volatility as a result of colder than normal weather.

1 BGSS incentive savings represent value created through supply and capacity optimization and shared with customers through the BGSS clause.

For more information on utility gross margin, please see "Non-GAAP Financial Information" below.

Energy-Efficiency Programs:

  • SAVEGREEN® invested $101.0 million in fiscal 2026 in energy-efficiency upgrades for customers' homes and businesses. Investments in SAVEGREEN® are incremental to rate base and earn near-real time returns through an annual recovery mechanism.
  • More than 115,000 customers have taken part in SAVEGREEN® to date, with those utilizing our whole home offerings realizing bill savings of up to 30%.

Clean Energy Ventures (CEV)
CEV reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter NFE of $33.5 million, compared with $23.8 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, reflecting higher Renewable Energy Credits and electricity revenue, partially offset by higher depreciation and interest expense associated with capital invested over the past year.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $37.6 million, compared with NFE of $61.2 million in fiscal 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a gain from the sale of CEV's residential solar portfolio assets that was recognized in the prior year period.

Solar Investment Update:

  • As of September 30, 2026, CEV had approximately 552 MW of commercial solar capacity in service across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Indiana, Michigan and Maine.

About New Jersey Resources

New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a diversified energy infrastructure and energy services company headquartered in Wall, New Jersey.

NJR is composed of five primary businesses:

  • New Jersey Natural Gas, NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties.
  • Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions.
  • Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America.
  • Storage and Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River and the Adelphia Gateway pipeline, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility.
  • Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey.

NJR and its almost 1,400 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as SAVEGREEN®.

NFE and financial margin exclude unrealized gains or losses on derivative instruments related to NJR’s unregulated subsidiaries and certain realized gains and losses on derivative instruments related to natural gas that has been placed into storage at ES, net of applicable tax adjustments as described below. Financial margin also differs from gross margin as defined on a GAAP basis as it excludes certain operations and maintenance expense and depreciation and amortization expenses as well as the effects of derivatives as discussed above. Volatility associated with the change in value of these financial instruments and physical commodity reported on the income statement in the current period. NJNG’s utility gross margin is defined as operating revenues less natural gas purchases, sales tax and regulatory rider expenses. Utility gross margin may also not be comparable to the definition of gross margin used by others in the natural gas distribution business and other industries. Management believes that utility gross margin provides a meaningful basis for evaluating utility operations since natural gas costs, sales tax and regulatory rider expenses are included in operating revenues and passed through to customers and, therefore, have no effect on utility gross margin.

Approval based on Phase 3 NIMBLE results demonstrating rapid, deep and sustained disease control that is maintained throughout three-month dosing intervals

Livsayis is Regeneron's first approved siRNA therapy and neurology medicine

TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive, the predominant form of the disease. Livsayis is a novel, complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of the disease. It is the first and only approved siRNA therapy in gMG and the only FDA-approved gMG treatment administered subcutaneously four times a year.

“For people living with gMG, every day can be unpredictable, due to fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigue. They may also experience severe exacerbations that can be life-threatening. Many still experience suboptimal disease control, whether from waning of therapeutic effect, inadequate response or high treatment burden,” said Tuan Vu, M.D., Professor of Neurology at the University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine, Division Director for Neuromuscular Medicine and EMG Laboratories, and a global principal investigator of the NIMBLE trial. “In the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, Livsayis delivered rapid, deep disease control – maintained through the end of dosing intervals – and offers a four-times-a-year subcutaneous dosing schedule. These results highlight how a first-of-its-kind approach can address a key driver of disease and provide a compelling treatment option.”

The FDA approval was based on results from the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial. Livsayis demonstrated the following least square mean change from baseline:

  • 4.5-point improvement on the Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) total score at 24 weeks (0.4 standard error [SE]) compared to a 2.2-point improvement with placebo (0.5 SE). This corresponded to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.3 points (p=0.0005). MG-ADL is a clinician-administered patient-reported assessment of daily functions impacted by gMG, such as talking, chewing, swallowing, breathing, vision and mobility. The proportion of MG-ADL responders with at least 3-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (76.6%) compared to placebo (44.1%, p<0.001).
  • 4.2-point improvement in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) total score at 24 weeks (0.6 SE) compared to a 1.5-point improvement with placebo (0.7 SE), corresponding to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.8 points (p=0.0015). QMG is a clinician-administered assessment of muscle function, including vision, speaking/swallowing, breathing and limb mobility. The proportion of QMG responders with at least a 5-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (48.4%) compared to placebo (19.0%, p<0.001).
  • Rapid onset of clinically meaningful benefit in MG-ADL (2.5 points), with improvements seen as early as two weeks of starting treatment that deepened over time.
  • Sustained disease control and symptom relief through 24 weeks, with MG-ADL scores maintained and no indication of waning efficacy.

The prescribing information for Livsayis includes a Boxed Warning for serious meningococcal infections in addition to warnings and precautions for other serious infections, consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in patients treated with Livsayis and more frequently than placebo were injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections. Livsayis is available only through a restricted program called the Livsayis Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), which is also consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. Details of the Important Safety Information are included below.

“Livsayis is Regeneron’s first approved medicine in neurology, and an important new option for people living with generalized myasthenia gravis who need effective disease control without a heavy treatment burden,” said George D. Yancopoulos, M.D., Ph.D., Board Co-Chair, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Regeneron. “As Regeneron’s first approved siRNA therapy, this approval marks a meaningful step forward for our neuroscience pipeline as we relentlessly pursue bold, new approaches to transform care for people living with serious neurological diseases.”

“Individuals living with gMG experience profound muscle weakness that can affect how they talk, see, breathe and move, and with it their ability to carry out everyday activities,” said Samantha Masterson, President & CEO, Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. “This approval is a positive milestone for the gMG community, reflecting continued progress on outcomes that matter most to patients. With Livsayis, those living with generalized myasthenia gravis have a new option that may help maintain disease control while reducing the burden treatment can place on daily life.”

Regeneron is committed to supporting people living with rare diseases and ensuring patients who have been prescribed Livsayis access to their medication. Regeneron’s myRARE™ program offers resources to help patients and healthcare providers, including product information, insurance benefit verification, and information about potential financial support. To learn about myRARE, visit myRARE.com or call 1-833-4my-RARE (1-833-469-7273).

A regulatory submission for Livsayis for the treatment of gMG is currently under review in the European Union, with a decision anticipated in the second half of 2027. Regulatory submissions are planned in additional markets, including Japan.

About gMG
gMG is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by unpredictable, debilitating and potentially life-threatening muscle weakness. In the most common form of the disease, abnormal anti-AChR antibodies activate the complement system including C5, disrupting communication between nerves and muscles, which contributes to damage at the neuromuscular junction. For these patients, the disease affects muscles throughout the body, resulting in extreme fatigue and difficulties with facial expression, speech, swallowing, mobility, breathing as well as severe exacerbations, including myasthenic crisis that can impair breathing to the point of requiring hospitalization. Worldwide, an estimated 150 to 200 out of every million people have MG. In the U.S., the disease impacts approximately 85,000 people.

About Livsayis
Livsayis is the first approved siRNA therapy for gMG and the only gMG treatment FDA-approved to be administered subcutaneously four times per year (every three months).

Livsayis is a complement C5-directed siRNA that degrades the messenger RNA (mRNA) that encodes the C5 protein, thereby blocking C5 production, reducing circulating levels of C5 and inhibiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of AChR-positive gMG.

Regeneron is solely responsible for the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of Livsayis through a worldwide licensing agreement with Alnylam.

About the NIMBLE trial
NIMBLE is the largest global, interventional gMG trial conducted to date. In this ongoing Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, Livsayis is being evaluated in patients with anti-AChR antibody-positive gMG who can continue background immunosuppressants based on the investigator’s discretion. Participants were randomized to receive one of four subcutaneous regimens: Livsayis every three months; a combination of Livsayis and a C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; or placebo every 4 weeks.

The primary endpoint assessed changes in the MG-ADL total score from baseline to week 24. The MG-ADL scale is an eight-question clinician-administered, patient-reported tool that measures how gMG affects aspects of daily life and provides a total score ranging from 0 to 24. The key secondary endpoint was the change from baseline in QMG total score at week 24. The QMG is a clinician-administered 13-item standardized assessment evaluating muscle function that provides a total score ranging from 0 to 39. In both MG-ADL and QMG, a higher total score indicates greater disease severity, and a larger reduction in total score indicates greater improvement in disease symptoms and better treatment effect.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a medicine that affects part of your immune system. LIVSAYIS may lower the ability of your immune system to fight certain infections.

  • LIVSAYIS increases your chance of getting serious meningococcal infections caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria. Meningococcal infections may quickly become life-threatening or cause death if not recognized and treated early.
    • You must complete your meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before your first dose of LIVSAYIS.
    • If you have not completed your meningococcal vaccines, and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you should receive the required vaccines as soon as possible.
    • If you have not been vaccinated and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you must also receive antibiotics.
    • If you had a meningococcal vaccine in the past, you might need additional vaccination before starting LIVSAYIS. Your healthcare provider will decide if you need additional meningococcal vaccination.
    • Meningococcal vaccines do not prevent all meningococcal infections. Call your healthcare provider or get emergency medical help right away if you get any of these signs and symptoms of a meningococcal infection: fever, fever and a rash, fever with high heart rate, headache with nausea or vomiting, headache and a fever, headache with a stiff neck or stiff back, confusion, muscle aches with flu-like symptoms, or eyes sensitive to light

Your healthcare provider will give you a Patient Safety Card about the risk of serious meningococcal infection. Carry it with you at all times during treatment and for 12 months after your last LIVSAYIS dose. Your risk of meningococcal infection may continue for several months after your last dose of LIVSAYIS. It is important to show this card to any healthcare provider who treats you. This will help them diagnose and treat you quickly.

LIVSAYIS is only available through a program called the LIVSAYIS Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). Before you can receive LIVSAYIS, your healthcare provider must: enroll in the LIVSAYIS REMS program; counsel you about the risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you the Patient Guide that explains your risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you a Patient Safety Card that has important information about the signs and symptoms of meningococcal infections; make sure that you are vaccinated against serious infections caused by meningococcal bacteria, and that you receive antibiotics if you need to start LIVSAYIS right away and you are not up-to-date on your vaccines.

LIVSAYIS may also increase the risk of other types of serious infections especially those caused by encapsulated bacteria, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Certain people may be at risk of serious infections with gonorrhea. Talk to your healthcare provider about whether you are at risk for gonorrhea infection, about gonorrhea prevention, and regular testing.

Call your healthcare provider right away if you have new signs or symptoms of infection.

Who should not receive LIVSAYIS?

  • Do not receive LIVSAYIS if you have a serious meningococcal infection when you are starting LIVSAYIS treatment.

Before you receive LIVSAYIS, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:

  • Have an infection or fever
  • Are pregnant or plan to be pregnant. It is not known whether LIVSAYIS will harm your unborn baby
  • Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if LIVSAYIS passes into your breast milk

Tell your healthcare provider about medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Know the medicines you take and the vaccines you receive. Keep a list of them to show your healthcare provider and pharmacist when you get a new medicine.

The most common side effects in people with gMG treated with LIVSAYIS include: injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections.
Tell your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or that does not go away. These are not all the possible side effects of LIVSAYIS. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Please see full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, and Medication Guide for LIVSAYIS.

What is LIVSAYIS?
LIVSAYIS is a prescription medicine used to treat a disease called generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive.

It is not known if LIVSAYIS is safe and effective in children.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Montfort Capital Corp. (TSXV: MONT) ("Montfort" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026 and second quarter ended June 30, 2026. All figures are reported in Canadian dollars unless otherwise noted.

"The first and second quarter results continue to illustrate the trajectory of our financial performance, driven by growth in the loan portfolios of Langhaus and Nuvo and ongoing careful management of expenses," said Ken Thomson, CEO of Montfort. "We are now generating consistent positive cash flow from operations that is sufficient to support our substantially reduced overhead and reinvest in our lending portfolios. I would like to extend my sincere gratitude to our operating team, board of directors and financial partners whose effort and commitment has been fundamental to achieving these significantly improved results."

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

For the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 the Company reports the following highlights:



To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12878/324754_85a1c703f41149f1_001full.jpg

Three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $0.5 million or 75% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.0 million increase in interest income on a larger loan portfolio, partially offset by a $0.6 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.2 million or 16% compared to the prior year, mainly due to lower administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.1 million) and amortization ($0.1 million), partially offset by a $0.1 million increase in accounting and legal fees.

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $5.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $0.6 million in the prior year, an improvement of $0.7 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $6.1 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million (sold April 2, 2025).

Six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $1.1 million or 101% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.8 million increase in interest income from loan growth in Langhaus and Nuvo, partially offset by a $1.0 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.9 million or 32% compared to the prior year, primarily due to reductions in administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.3 million), amortization ($0.2 million), bad debts ($0.2 million) and share-based payments ($0.1 million).

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $0.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $1.8 million in the prior year, an improvement of $1.8 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $2.4 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million, partially offset by operating losses of Brightpath and Pivot, including expected credit losses of $5.7 million.

  • Loans receivable as at June 30, 2026, net of allowance, increased by $27.6 million or 13% compared to the balance at December 31, 2025, driven by loan growth in Langhaus ($18.2 million) and Nuvo ($9.4 million). Advances of $58.3 million were partially offset by settlements of $30.6 million.

This news release is qualified in its entirety by the Company's financial statements for the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and the associated Management's Discussion & Analysis, which can be downloaded from the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at https://www.sedarplus.ca/

About Montfort Capital Corp.

Montfort builds and manages private credit portfolios that have focused investing strategies for the institutional and accredited investors markets. For further information, please visit www.montfortcapital.com.

The Company originates, underwrites and manages secured loans through the following operating divisions:

Continuing Operations

Langhaus provides insurance policy-backed lending solutions to high-net-worth individuals and entrepreneurs in Canada. Langhaus' loans are collateralized by the assignment of the borrower's whole life insurance policy, personal and/or corporate guarantees and, in some cases, other tangible collateral.

Nuvo partners with Canadian alternative asset managers and ultra high-net-worth individuals to provide revolving net asset value based loans (ie. 'NAV loans').

Discontinued Operations

The Brightpath business was sold on April 2, 2025. Brightpath is a registered mortgage brokerage and mortgage administrator, administering a portfolio of mortgages secured by residential properties. As at December 31, 2024, the assets and liabilities of Brightpath were classified as held for sale and the operating results are included under discontinued operations up to the date of sale.

The Pivot business was sold on November 4, 2025. Pivot specializes in asset-based lending targeting SME borrowers in Canada. Sources of revenue include net interest income from loans receivable, origination fees and amendment fees. In addition, Pivot earns loan servicing fees and performance fee income for loan management services performed.
